sample_unit: AI-generated explanations (plus 15 expert reviewers and 54 patient survey participants)

links.outcome: Readability of AI explanations versus original clinician notes (FK grade, Flesch Reading Ease, Gunning Fog)
links.effect: FK Grade Level fell 10.57 to 7.61; Flesch Reading Ease rose 37.7 to 69.6; Gunning Fog fell 14.5 to 10.4; all P ≤ 0.002.
links.quote: AI-generated explanations demonstrated consistent improvements in readability, with mean Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level decreasing by 2.96 levels (10.57-7.61), Flesch Reading Ease increasing by 31.9 points (37.7-69.6), and Gunning Fog Index decreasing by 4.09 points (14.5-10.4); all improvements were statistically significant (all P ≤ 0.002).

links.outcome: Grade-level reduction by intended audience adaptation (child, teenager, adult, carer)
links.effect: Readability gains were greatest for younger audiences: child 4.25 grade-level reduction versus adult 1.80.
links.quote: Readability gains were greatest for younger audiences (child: 4.25 grade-level reduction; adult: 1.80).

unlisted_practices: Audience-specific and tone-specific (friendly, informative, reassuring) adaptation of LLM explanations of clinician-authored notes
Deliberately constraining an LLM patient tool to language simplification without clinical interpretation

screen.reason: Evaluates a patient-facing LLM application (Patiently AI) for simplifying clinical notes via readability metrics, clinician safety/accuracy review, and patient comprehension surveys.
